title: Ja'far's speech
hookLine: Ja'far explains to the Negus: we lived in ignorance and cruelty, then a man came teaching truth, kinship and mercy (sirah)

cards: Two envoys from Quraysh arrive at the Negus's court with gifts of leather, and something for each of the king's patricians first. Their request: these runaways have abandoned our religion and haven't taken yours.
Hand them back. The patricians agree. But the king won't hand anyone over without hearing them.

So the Muslims are summoned, and they must decide quickly what to say. Umm Salamah, who was there, says they agreed: we will say what we know, and what our Prophet told us, whatever comes of it. Today: Ja'far's speech.

teach.b: The one who speaks for them is Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's cousin. Umm Salamah's report, kept in Musnad Ahmad, gives the speech; here it is in paraphrase. O king, we were a people living in ignorance.
We worshipped idols, ate dead animals, did shameful things, cut our ties of family, treated our neighbors badly, and the strong among us devoured the weak.

teach.h: A MAN WHOSE TRUTHFULNESS WE KNEW.
teach.b: Then God sent us a messenger from among us, whose family, truthfulness, trustworthiness and purity we knew. He called us to worship God alone and leave the stones our fathers had served.
He told us to speak the truth, keep our trusts, hold to our kin, be good to our neighbors, and stop the bloodshed.
Then our own people turned on us, so we came to your land, choosing you, hoping not to be wronged near you. Listen to how it's built. It doesn't start with doctrine.
It starts with a confession: this is what we were.

Then the change, and the change is mostly about how people treat each other: truth, trust, family, neighbors, the weak. Today's line names three threads of it: truth, kinship, mercy. And notice what he leaves out.
He doesn't insult the envoys, their gods, or the king's faith.

teach.h: NO INSULTS. A BEFORE AND AFTER.
teach.b: He tells a before and after, and lets the king judge.

how: Muslims retell Ja'far's speech to the Negus in sirah lessons and sermons as a summary of what the Prophet's message changed in his community's way of living.

games.q: you're one of the emigrants, summoned before the king. the envoys want you sent back. what will you say?
o: what we know and what our Prophet told us, whatever comes.
games.why: Umm Salamah says they agreed to say what they knew, whatever came of it; Ja'far spoke for them.

practice: Find three sentences about your values, without hurrying: one for where you came from, one for what changed you, or who, and one for how you now try to treat people.
No big words, no argument, just the way you'd say them to a stranger who had the power to send you away. Say them once in your head, then once softly aloud.

wordCard.voice: Ja'far's speech. Before the Negus, Ja'far tells what his people were, who came to them, and what he taught: truth, trust, kinship, neighbors, an end to bloodshed. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Ja'far son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's cousin, who spoke for the emigrants.

carryVoice: Your line: truth, kinship, mercy. A before and an after, and not one insult. Day seven hundred forty-three.
